applications</div></div><div class="flex flex-col gap-v2/12"><div class="type-md-lg text-theme-text">Daily</div><div class="type-sm text-theme-text-sec leading-[var(--leading-cozy)]">Deployment cadence, up from monthly release cycle</div></div></div></div></div></div></aside><div class="prose prose--block prose--blog col-span-full! prose-dropcap"><p>PayPal has its startup energy again.</p>
<p>Here&#x27;s one measure of the change: PayPal recently completed a Java upgrade across 3,000 applications in two months. Previously it would have taken eight to twelve months. With 8,000 developers and a codebase spanning decades, that kind of acceleration seemed impossible.</p>
<p>But it&#x27;s happening because of how the company adopted Cursor.</p>
<div class="not-prose my-6"><div class="card"><p class="type-base text-theme-text mb-6 whitespace-pre-line">For the first time we&#x27;re able to see a real path to being as scrappy as a startup, but with all the funding and maturity of a large enterprise.</p><div><div class="type-sm text-theme-text">Michelle Chance</div><div class="type-sm text-theme-text-sec">Head of Developer Platforms, PayPal</div></div></div></div>
<h2 id="start-with-high-impact-teams" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#start-with-high-impact-teams" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Start with high-impact teams</h2>
<p>PayPal recognized early on that AI needed to be an intrinsic part of its products and how it worked. But it also needed to move carefully. The company moves money for more than 400 million customers around the world, and the cost of mistakes is high.</p>
<p>So when they rolled out Cursor, they started with their highest-impact teams building the most impactful products where speed to market was essential. Within two weeks, those teams were deploying daily instead of weekly or biweekly.</p>
<div class="not-prose my-6"><div class="card"><p class="type-base text-theme-text mb-6 whitespace-pre-line">Cursor has been critical in accelerating our timelines from doing something in four sprints to getting it done in one.</p><div><div class="type-sm text-theme-text">Michelle Chance</div><div class="type-sm text-theme-text-sec">Head of Developer Platforms, PayPal</div></div></div></div>
<p>Adoption spread organically across the organization as engineers saw what their peers were accomplishing with Cursor. Teams with high Cursor adoption rates—many exceeding 90%—showed dramatic improvements in deployment frequency and lead time.</p>
<div class="not-prose my-6"><div class="card"><p class="type-base text-theme-text mb-6 whitespace-pre-line">Teams with high adoption are deploying faster and shipping with shorter lead times.</p><div><div class="type-sm text-theme-text">Michelle Chance</div><div class="type-sm text-theme-text-sec">Head of Developer Platforms, PayPal</div></div></div></div>
<h2 id="new-ways-of-working" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#new-ways-of-working" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>New ways of working</h2>
<p>Software development has fundamentally changed too. The old linear software development lifecycle—design, code, build, deploy—has given way to something more iterative. Teams move from idea to working prototype in hours, then iterate from there.</p>
<p>That process has collapsed traditional role boundaries. Product managers are bringing functioning prototypes to engineers instead of just PRDs while engineers are replying with their own prototypes of what the product could look like.</p>
<div class="not-prose my-6"><div class="card"><p class="type-base text-theme-text mb-6 whitespace-pre-line">Roles that used to be very finite are blurring and we&#x27;re seeing better product ideas come out of it.</p><div><div class="type-sm text-theme-text">Michelle Chance</div><div class="type-sm text-theme-text-sec">Head of Developer Platforms, PayPal</div></div></div></div>
<p>This shift, in process and in how roles are defined, is changing what matters in engineering. Now it&#x27;s much more about creativity and problem-solving.</p>
<p>Prakhar Mehrotra, Global Head of AI at PayPal, compares engineers using Cursor to superheroes who can move beyond hypersonic speeds but still have to decide where to apply their powers.</p>
<div class="not-prose my-6"><div class="card"><p class="type-base text-theme-text mb-6 whitespace-pre-line">Engineers still have to decide what problem to solve. But you&#x27;re getting there much faster.</p><div><div class="type-sm text-theme-text">Prakhar Mehrotra</div><div class="type-sm text-theme-text-sec">SVP, Global Head of AI, PayPal</div></div></div></div>
<h2 id="measuring-what-matters" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#measuring-what-matters" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Measuring what matters</h2>
<p>While the way PayPal builds software has changed, the company has continued measuring what has always mattered: deployment frequency, lead time from idea to production, change failure rate. They also deliberately avoid metrics that could distort how people work.</p>
<div class="not-prose my-6"><div class="card"><p class="type-base text-theme-text mb-6 whitespace-pre-line">If you measure it, you impact it. If you tell a developer their success is based on what percentage of code was generated by AI, they&#x27;ll just ask AI to write verbose functions.</p><div><div class="type-sm text-theme-text">Michelle Chance</div><div class="type-sm text-theme-text-sec">Head of Developer Platforms, PayPal</div></div></div></div>
<p>Teams with high Cursor adoption are deploying multiple times per day instead of once per week. Lead times have shrunk. Change failure rates have dropped.</p>
<p>Based on those metrics, Chance believes PayPal could even be ready to deliver 40% more capabilities in 2026 than it shipped in 2025.</p>
<h2 id="the-intelligence-shift" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#the-intelligence-shift" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>The intelligence shift</h2>
<p>Mehrotra sees what&#x27;s happening at PayPal as the leading edge of a larger shift. The last 20 years were about organizing and distributing information. Something different is underway now.</p>
<div class="not-prose my-6"><div class="card"><p class="type-base text-theme-text mb-6 whitespace-pre-line">AI is about intelligence, not information. It&#x27;s a fundamentally different technology stack.</p><div><div class="type-sm text-theme-text">Prakhar Mehrotra</div><div class="type-sm text-theme-text-sec">SVP, Global Head of AI, PayPal</div></div></div></div>
<p>A fast, full embrace of that shift is allowing PayPal to transform its business, from payments to commerce more broadly. That expanded sense of possibility is pulling engineers in and making them want to contribute to what PayPal is doing.</p>
<div class="not-prose my-6"><div class="card"><p class="type-base text-theme-text mb-6 whitespace-pre-line">The most important thing is our developers are participating in the AI journey. They want to come work for us because PayPal supports tools like Cursor.</p><div><div class="type-sm text-theme-text">Prakhar Mehrotra</div><div class="type-sm text-theme-text-sec">SVP, Global Head of AI, PayPal</div></div></div></div>
<hr/>
<p>If you&#x27;re excited about leveraging agents to transform your engineering team&#x27;s velocity, please <a href="https://cursor.com/contact-sales?source=customers" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">reach out to our team</a> to start a free Cursor trial.</p></div><footer class="mt-v2"><p class="type-base"><span class="text-theme-text-sec">Filed under:<!-- --> </span><a Asia-Pacific.</p><div class="not-prose mb-8 mb-0 mt-v1"><div class="pb-g1.75"><div class="border-theme-border-02 flex flex-col gap-v1 border-l-2 pl-g1.5 pb-[2px]"><div class="flex flex-col class="flex flex-col gap-v2/12"><div class="type-md-lg text-theme-text">6x</div><div class="type-sm text-theme-text-sec leading-[var(--leading-cozy)]">Faster Java upgrade across 3,000 applications</div></div><div class="flex flex-col gap-v2/12"><div class="type-md-lg text-theme-text">Daily</div><div class="type-sm text-theme-text-sec leading-[var(--leading-cozy)]">Deployment cadence, up from monthly release cycle</div></div></div></div></div></div></aside><div class="prose prose--block prose--blog col-span-full! prose-dropcap"><p>PayPal has its startup energy again.</p>
<p>Here&#x27;s one measure of the change: PayPal recently completed a Java upgrade across 3,000 applications in two months. Previously it would have taken eight to twelve months. With 8,000 developers and a codebase spanning decades, that kind of acceleration seemed impossible.</p>
<p>But it&#x27;s happening because of how the company adopted Cursor.</p>
<div class="not-prose my-6"><div class="card"><p class="type-base text-theme-text mb-6 whitespace-pre-line">For the first time we&#x27;re able to see a real path to being as scrappy as a startup, but with all the funding and maturity of a large enterprise.</p><div><div class="type-sm text-theme-text">Michelle Chance</div><div class="type-sm text-theme-text-sec">Head of Developer Platforms, PayPal</div></div></div></div>
<h2 id="start-with-high-impact-teams" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#start-with-high-impact-teams" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Start with high-impact teams</h2>
<p>PayPal recognized early on that AI needed to be an intrinsic part of its products and how it worked. But it also needed to move carefully. The company moves money for more than 400 million customers around the world, and the cost of mistakes is high.</p>
<p>So when they rolled out Cursor, they started with their highest-impact teams building the most impactful products where speed to market was essential. Within two weeks, those teams were deploying daily instead of weekly or biweekly.</p>
<div class="not-prose my-6"><div class="card"><p class="type-base text-theme-text mb-6 whitespace-pre-line">Cursor has been critical in accelerating our timelines from doing something in four sprints to getting it done in one.</p><div><div class="type-sm text-theme-text">Michelle Chance</div><div class="type-sm text-theme-text-sec">Head of Developer Platforms, PayPal</div></div></div></div>
<p>Adoption spread organically across the organization as engineers saw what their peers were accomplishing with Cursor. Teams with high Cursor adoption rates—many exceeding 90%—showed dramatic improvements in deployment frequency and lead time.</p>
<div class="not-prose my-6"><div class="card"><p class="type-base text-theme-text mb-6 whitespace-pre-line">Teams with high adoption are deploying faster and shipping with shorter lead times.</p><div><div class="type-sm text-theme-text">Michelle Chance</div><div class="type-sm text-theme-text-sec">Head of Developer Platforms, PayPal</div></div></div></div>
<h2 id="new-ways-of-working" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#new-ways-of-working" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>New ways of working</h2>
<p>Software development has fundamentally changed too. The old linear software development lifecycle—design, code, build, deploy—has given way to something more iterative. Teams move from idea to working prototype in hours, then iterate from there.</p>
<p>That process has collapsed traditional role boundaries. Product managers are bringing functioning prototypes to engineers instead of just PRDs while engineers are replying with their own prototypes of what the product could look like.</p>
<div class="not-prose my-6"><div class="card"><p class="type-base text-theme-text mb-6 whitespace-pre-line">Roles that used to be very finite are blurring and we&#x27;re seeing better product ideas come out of it.</p><div><div class="type-sm text-theme-text">Michelle Chance</div><div class="type-sm text-theme-text-sec">Head of Developer Platforms, PayPal</div></div></div></div>
<p>This shift, in process and in how roles are defined, is changing what matters in engineering. Now it&#x27;s much more about creativity and problem-solving.</p>
<p>Prakhar Mehrotra, Global Head of AI at PayPal, compares engineers using Cursor to superheroes who can move beyond hypersonic speeds but still have to decide where to apply their powers.</p>
<div class="not-prose my-6"><div class="card"><p class="type-base text-theme-text mb-6 whitespace-pre-line">Engineers still have to decide what problem to solve. But you&#x27;re getting there much faster.</p><div><div class="type-sm text-theme-text">Prakhar Mehrotra</div><div class="type-sm text-theme-text-sec">SVP, Global Head of AI, PayPal</div></div></div></div>
<h2 id="measuring-what-matters" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#measuring-what-matters" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Measuring what matters</h2>
<p>While the way PayPal builds software has changed, the company has continued measuring what has always mattered: deployment frequency, lead time from idea to production, change failure rate. They also deliberately avoid metrics that could distort how people work.</p>
<div class="not-prose my-6"><div class="card"><p class="type-base text-theme-text mb-6 whitespace-pre-line">If you measure it, you impact it. If you tell a developer their success is based on what percentage of code was generated by AI, they&#x27;ll just ask AI to write verbose functions.</p><div><div class="type-sm text-theme-text">Michelle Chance</div><div class="type-sm text-theme-text-sec">Head of Developer Platforms, PayPal</div></div></div></div>
<p>Teams with high Cursor adoption are deploying multiple times per day instead of once per week. Lead times have shrunk. Change failure rates have dropped.</p>
<p>Based on those metrics, Chance believes PayPal could even be ready to deliver 40% more capabilities in 2026 than it shipped in 2025.</p>
<h2 id="the-intelligence-shift" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#the-intelligence-shift" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>The intelligence shift</h2>
<p>Mehrotra sees what&#x27;s happening at PayPal as the leading edge of a larger shift. The last 20 years were about organizing and distributing information. Something different is underway now.</p>
<div class="not-prose my-6"><div class="card"><p class="type-base text-theme-text mb-6 whitespace-pre-line">AI is about intelligence, not information. It&#x27;s a fundamentally different technology stack.</p><div><div class="type-sm text-theme-text">Prakhar Mehrotra</div><div class="type-sm text-theme-text-sec">SVP, Global Head of AI, PayPal</div></div></div></div>
<p>A fast, full embrace of that shift is allowing PayPal to transform its business, from payments to commerce more broadly. That expanded sense of possibility is pulling engineers in and making them want to contribute to what PayPal is doing.</p>
<div class="not-prose my-6"><div class="card"><p class="type-base text-theme-text mb-6 whitespace-pre-line">The most important thing is our developers are participating in the AI journey. They want to come work for us because PayPal supports tools like Cursor.</p><div><div class="type-sm text-theme-text">Prakhar Mehrotra</div><div class="type-sm text-theme-text-sec">SVP, Global Head of AI, PayPal</div></div></div></div>
<hr/>
<p>If you&#x27;re excited about leveraging agents to transform your engineering team&#x27;s velocity, please <a href="https://cursor.com/contact-sales?source=customers" rel="noopener noreferrer"
